external_entities.name: developers
external_entities.description: Developers who push branches to the self-hosted git server and can manually start a rebuild of main.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
external_entities.notes: Any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of main by hand.

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves the dependency lockfile, produces container images, pushes images to the image registry, calls the deploy controller, and can be used to manually rebuild main.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network. It does not verify signatures on downloads from the public package registry.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Receives the requested image release from the build runner and serves the current release to store servers.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network
processes.notes: The controller holds one record identifying which image sha the estate should be on.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small server in the back office of each store that runs the till software as a container, polls the deploy controller, pulls images, and restarts the container when the release changes.
processes.source_excerpt: Each store has a small server in the back office running the till software as a container.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: Software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container

data_stores.name: self-hosted git server
data_stores.description: A self-hosted git server on the corporate network that receives developer branches and provides source for builds.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: A registry in the build environment that stores finished container images tagged with commit sha and serves images to store servers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores. The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.

data_stores.name: current release
data_stores.description: The record held by the deploy controller identifying which image sha the estate should be running.
data_stores.source_excerpt: holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on

data_flows.name: pushes branches
data_flows.description: Developers push their branches to the self-hosted git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: fetches source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source from the self-hosted git server after a merge.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source

data_flows.name: starts build
data_flows.description: A merge to main starts a build on the build runner.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A merge to `main` is what starts a build.

data_flows.name: kicks off rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer can log in to the build runner and manually kick off a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

data_flows.name: resolves dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches out to the public package registry during dependency resolution.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.

data_flows.name: pushes image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit sha.
data_flows.data_description: finished container image tagged with commit sha

data_flows.name: requests release
data_flows.description: After pushing an image, the build runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When the image is pushed the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.

data_flows.name: polls release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pulls image
data_flows.description: When the current release differs from the running release, a store server pulls the image from the registry and restarts the container.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry and restarts the container
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.
data_flows.data_description: container image for the current release

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network containing the self-hosted git server and deploy controller.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The separate build environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The networked estate of store servers across about 1,200 stores.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet reached during dependency resolution.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: Developers are assigned to the corporate network boundary for modelling their interaction with the corporate git server.
assumptions.basis: The source places the self-hosted git server on the corporate network but does not state where developers are located.

assumptions.assumption: The public package registry is assigned to the internet boundary.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly describes the public package registry as being on the internet.
